title: Rewrite pre-canonical architecture epics before execution
description: Execution controller for rewriting the two highest-priority pre-canonical architecture epics so they fit the goal-state Wheelwright model before any implementation is attempted from them. This batch is planning-heavy but still uses an implementation-control lug so review, remediation, and acceptance stay on one durable object.
non_goals: Do not implement skills-folder architecture in code in this batch
Do not implement working-agreement behavior in code in this batch
Do not broaden into sharded-lug storage or post-evolution skills in this batch
Do not leave conversation-only rewrite decisions; persist them in the lugs

must_be_sequential: 1. Review goal-state design, legacy-lug rewrite map, and current canonical epic before editing lugs.
2. Rewrite epic-skills-folder-architecture so it describes a canonical-compatible direction or is explicitly deferred if it conflicts with the small-core-object model.
3. Rewrite epic-working-agreement-skill so it fits the current skill/advisor model without reviving _critical_directives-era assumptions.
4. Add clear execution conditions, non-goals, and dependencies so future implementers do not pick up stale assumptions.
5. Update this lug with what was rewritten, what was deferred, and what remains blocked on later canonical stabilization.
can_parallelize: Read-only stale-language inventory for each target epic before editing
Draft rewrite notes for the two epics separately before final reconciliation
blocked_until: If runtime-baseline and state/migration semantics are still unstable, avoid claiming final architecture details that depend on them
If review shows one epic should be archived instead of rewritten, stop and return to user rather than forcing a rewrite
later_batches: Any code implementation implied by the rewritten epics
Post-evolution skills like check-spokes and dogfood
Docs rewrite once runtime and architecture records are stable

review_questions: Does the rewrite remove stale teach/learn, BRIEF/Manifest, or shell-command assumptions?
Does the rewritten epic align with the small-core-object and skill/advisor model?
Is execution deferred where the canonical system is not yet stable enough?
Would a future implementer understand the new boundaries without chat context?
implementer_review.approval_rule: Persist review outcome before editing the epic lugs. If an epic should be archived or split rather than rewritten, return to user with that recommendation first.

recommended_uses: Read-only stale-language inventory on the target epics
Narrow consistency checks against the legacy-lug rewrite map
not_safe_for: Turning a planning rewrite into code implementation
Broad discovery outside the target epics and canonical design sources

model_recommendations.primary_implementer: Use a strong reasoning model for architectural rewrite and boundary-setting

verification_requirements: Verify the rewritten epics no longer teach deprecated control-plane assumptions
Verify execution conditions and non-goals are explicit
Verify future implementation work can load the rewritten lugs without chat context
Record whether either epic was rewritten, deferred, split, or recommended for archival
